title: Why the difference: mortal falls quit covenant-necessary obedience; lighter faults do not
source_text: L. Hujus vero discriminis inter utriusque generis peccata rationem esse dicit, quod renati in atrocia, & conscientiam vastantia peccata prolapsi, praestare desinunt eam obedientiam quam foedus gratiae a nobis exigit, ut necessariam ad consequenda ulte-riora gratiae dona in hac vita, & ad obtinendam visionem Dei beatificam in vita fu-tura. Adeoque quamdiu fideles & renati gravibus & atrocibus illis peccatis impliciti manent, incapaces sunt istorum beneficiorum, non tantum demerito suo, sed etiam secundum sententiam foederis gratiae, donec per singularem, extraordinariam, & perfecte practicam poenitentiam ad Deum redeant, & omnem hujusmodi malignitatem actionum suarum ex adverso oculorum Dei amoveant. At quando electi & justificati leviora illa peccata, ex inadvertentia, aut infirmitate committunt, non desinunt prae-stare obedientiam illam, quam foedus gratiae, ut praecise necessariam ad salutem exigit. Atque iis non obstantibus, dicuntur secundum spiritum ambulare; imo & Deum toto corde sequi, & incedere in omnibus mandatis & constitutionibus Domini incul-pate.
pass_a_gloss: But the reason of this discrimination between sins of either kind he says is this: that the regenerate, having fallen into atrocious and conscience-wasting sins, cease to render that obedience which the covenant of grace exacts from us as necessary for obtaining further gifts of grace in this life and for obtaining the beatific vision of God in the life to come. And so long as the faithful and regenerate remain entangled in those grave and atrocious sins, they are incapable of those benefits, not only by their own demerit, but also according to the sentence of the covenant of grace, until by a singular, extraordinary, and perfectly practical repentance they return to God and remove all such malignity of their actions from before God’s eyes. But when the elect and justified commit those lighter sins from inadvertence or infirmity, they do not cease to render that obedience which the covenant of grace exacts as precisely necessary for salvation. And those things notwithstanding, they are said to walk according to the Spirit; nay even to follow God with the whole heart, and to walk in all the Lord’s commandments and ordinances blamelessly.
pass_b_english: Mortal falls break the obedience the grace-covenant requires for further gifts and the beatific vision—until extraordinary practical repentance.
Lighter infirmity-slips leave that precise salvation-obedience standing: Spirit-walk and whole-hearted following still named.
